_about: Interventions for water security and ecological restoration, shared by the watershed and waterbody atlases. Supply-side interventions add water (harvest, store, recharge, restore land that lets rain soak in); demand-side interventions reduce or reallocate use (crops, irrigation methods, rules and institutions). Each entry gives where it is built ('where', with the site rules of the CoRE Stack structure-suitability spreadsheet and the ridge-to-valley table of the watershed-development toolkit paper), the landscapes it suits ('landscape', 'archetypes'), a landscape fit test evaluated for each micro-watershed ('suits', 'avoid'), the watershed stresses and waterbody rules it responds to ('addresses', 'addresses_wb', limited to 'wb_types'), schemes that fund it, examples from civil society practice, and sources. Site rules apply to a specific site and need field checks; the fit test only says whether the micro-watershed's landscape is the kind where the intervention usually works.

sides.supply: Adds water or keeps it in the landscape: harvesting, storage, recharge, soil and land restoration.
sides.demand: Reduces or reallocates water use: crops, irrigation methods, rules, institutions and planning.

categories.drainage_line: Drainage-line treatment (across streams, by stream order)
categories.area_treatment: Area treatment on slopes and ridges (off drainage lines)
categories.restoration: Ecological restoration of commons, forest and banks

fit.about: Landscape fit for a micro-watershed (and, in the waterbody atlas, for the waterbody's home micro-watershed): 'suited' when 'suits' holds and 'avoid' does not; 'not suited' when 'avoid' holds; otherwise 'possible'. Expressions read the watershed variables (variables.json), the system shares (share_<archetype>), and the context classes as terrain, aquifer, rainfall, gw_category, canal and cropping. A missing value never makes an intervention suited or unsuited. In the waterbody atlas an intervention is shown for a waterbody only if its type is in 'wb_types' (when given).

levels.suited: The landscape is the kind where this intervention usually works; check the site rules on the ground.
levels.possible: Nothing in the data rules it in or out; decide from site rules and community knowledge.
levels.not suited: The landscape works against it (reason given); consider other interventions first.

community_vars.wl_post_monsoon: Depth to the water level in open wells after the monsoon (m), from the Commons Connect landscape question ls_wl_post; unknown until answered, and then an unknown value changes no verdict.

site_rules_about: Site rules start from the CoRE Stack 'Water structures — suitability rules' spreadsheet and were checked on 24 November 2026 against the CGWB Manual on Artificial Recharge (2007), the Gujarat IWMP technical manual (2011), the IMSD guidelines (NRSA 1995), NIH (Saha et al. 2018), ICAR-CRIDA's farm pond bulletin (2012), PRADAN's INRM handbook and the Tripura soil and moisture conservation guidelines. For each parameter: the accepted, partially accepted and not accepted range, and its basis: verified (a source agrees), revised (changed to what the sources give), added (a parameter the spreadsheet lacked) or spreadsheet (no published source found). Site rules are the layers read at the site itself: slope, stream order, catchment area, distance to the nearest drainage line, land use and soil (soil is not yet a CoRE Stack layer: the field worker records it with the Commons Connect soil classes). Rainfall, aquifer, groundwater stage and depth to water belong to the landscape fit ('suits' and 'avoid'); depth to water is asked of the community until a layer exists. Slope in %, catchment in hectares, distance to the nearest drainage line in metres, land use as the CoRE Stack land-use classes. 'site_spec' gives the ridge-to-valley placement.

interventions.name: Loose boulder checks
interventions.what: Small dry-stone barriers across first-order gullies and streams. They slow flash runoff, trap silt and let water soak in; the first treatment of a gully before larger structures downstream.
interventions.where: Drainage line, stream order 1 (up to 3), upper catchment

site_rules.note: Bed slope below 20%; the spreadsheet ranges (1–10% accepted, 6–20% partial) overlapped.
Gujarat: drainage lines under 50 ha, each structure with an independent catchment of 1–2 ha; height up to 1 m.

interventions.landscape: Hilly and undulating land with gullies: forest-fringe, pastoral and upland rainfed micro-watersheds; also above tanks that are silting up.
interventions.avoid_note: Almost no sloping land: few gullies to treat.
interventions.site_check: Revised against the Gujarat IWMP manual: catchment widened to 50 ha and the slope ranges made consistent.

interventions.name: Earthen and brushwood gully plugs
interventions.what: Earthen or brushwood plugs in small, steep gullies to stop gully head-cutting and hold silt; usually combined with vegetation on the plug.
interventions.where: Drainage line, stream order 1, steep upper slopes
interventions.site_spec: Earthen gully plugs: across first-order gullies on upper slopes, gully catchments up to 2 ha (medium gullies up to 20 ha), gully bed slopes of about 4–15%; under 2 m deep and 5 m wide

site_rules.note: Gully bed slopes in the Gujarat design table: brushwood 0–5%, earthen 4.5–10.5%, sandbag and masonry 7.5–15%.
CGWB: gully plugs are built across first-order streams.
Small gullies drain up to 2 ha and medium ones 2–20 ha; PRADAN: only gullies under 2 m deep and 5 m wide.

site_rules.not_accepted: Croplands; Built-up; water in any season

interventions.landscape: Steep, uncultivated slopes under scrub, forest or barren land: forest-fringe and commons-dominated micro-watersheds.
interventions.site_check: Revised against the CGWB and Gujarat manuals and PRADAN.

interventions.name: Gabion structures and rock-fill dams
interventions.what: Boulders packed in wire mesh (gabions) or loose rock-fill across second-order streams; flexible, they hold silt and raise local water tables where flows are too strong for loose boulders.
interventions.site_spec: Gabions / rock-fill dams: second-order streams 10–20 m wide with catchments of 30–150 ha; 1–2 m high, keyed into stable banks

site_rules.note: Gujarat: gabions for 30–150 ha catchments, 1–2 m high across streams 10–20 m wide.

site_rules.not_accepted: Trees/forest; Built-up; water in any season

interventions.landscape: Undulating to hilly land with second-order streams in scrub or barren catchments; where stone is available locally.
interventions.avoid_note: Flat: streams too slow for gabions to help.
interventions.site_check: Catchment revised against the Gujarat IWMP manual; the other rows are from the spreadsheet (no other source gives them).

interventions.name: Check dams, cement nala bunds and anicuts
interventions.what: Masonry or concrete weirs across seasonal streams that store water in the stream bed through the monsoon and recharge the aquifer; downstream wells and fields benefit (the paper estimates the downstream cropping area that a check dam protects).
interventions.where: Drainage line: seasonal streams of order 2 to 3, catchments of about 40 to 500 ha
interventions.site_spec: Check dams, cement nala bunds and anicuts: across a seasonal stream of order 2 to 3 with a catchment of 40 to 500 ha, a gentle bed slope (under about 5%), and a stable, impervious foundation with permeable weathered rock or alluvium upstream so that stored water recharges the aquifer. Larger catchments need a designed spillway and become a percolation tank or small dam

site_rules.note: A gentle bed slope stores more water behind a low wall.
Up to third order (NIH); IMSD allows 1–4; first-order channels take gully plugs and boulder checks.

site_rules.partial: 25–40 ha or 500–1000 ha (masonry check dams with a designed spillway)
site_rules.note: CGWB: 40–100 ha for check dams and cement nala bunds; IMSD and NIH: above 25 ha; Gujarat: masonry check dams normally 500–1000 ha.

site_rules.accepted: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping
site_rules.not_accepted: Trees/forest; Built-up; water in any season

site_rules.accepted: Red, Laterite, Alluvial over a sound foundation
site_rules.not_accepted: Rocky with open fractures under the wall
site_rules.note: Low to medium permeability under the wall holds the water; permeable strata upstream let it recharge (NIH; CGWB).

interventions.landscape: Hard-rock (basalt, granite, gneiss) micro-watersheds with seasonal streams and well-irrigated farms downstream; most useful where the weathered zone can take recharge. Least useful on flat alluvial plains with shallow water tables. As a recharge structure it suits areas with less than about 1000 mm of rain a year (CGWB); in wetter areas it is possible but mainly stores water for irrigation.
interventions.suits: (aquifer == 'hard_rock' or soge_stage >= 70) and f_slopy + f_hill >= 0.15 and nz(rain_norm) < 1000
interventions.avoid: (aquifer == 'alluvium' and terrain == 'plain' and nz(soge_stage) < 70 and rain_norm >= 1000) or (known(wl_post_monsoon) and wl_post_monsoon < 3)
interventions.avoid_note: Flat, humid alluvial plain with a shallow, safe water table: little room for extra recharge and a risk of waterlogging.
interventions.caution: Upstream structures cut inflow to tanks and check dams downstream (Wable et al. 2022); plan at micro-watershed scale and keep part of the runoff flowing. Desilt regularly.
practice: Saurashtra (Gujarat): check-dam and well-recharge movement of the 1990s, led by farmers and diamond merchants
Ralegan Siddhi and Hiware Bazar (Ahmednagar, Maharashtra): cement nala bunds and check dams with village rules on water use
Utthan, Bhavnagar (Gujarat): check dams in the paper's Morchand village plan
interventions.site_check: Checked against CGWB, IMSD, NIH (Saha et al. 2018) and the Gujarat IWMP manual: stream order narrowed to 2–3 and the lower catchment bound brought to 25 ha. Rainfall is part of the landscape fit, not the site rules.

interventions.name: Percolation tanks
interventions.what: Shallow tanks on second- and third-order streams sited over permeable strata so that stored water percolates to wells downstream within a few months, rather than being used directly.
interventions.where: Drainage line, stream order 2–3, gentle slopes

site_rules.note: Land slope at the tank site; IMSD allows percolation ponds up to 10%.
CGWB: 2.5–4 km² for small and 5–8 km² for large tanks; IMSD sites percolation ponds from 25 ha.

site_rules.accepted: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping
site_rules.not_accepted: Trees/forest; Built-up; water in any season

site_rules.accepted: Red, Laterite, Alluvial (coarse), Sandy over weathered or fractured rock
site_rules.note: The tank bed must be permeable so that stored water reaches the aquifer (CGWB; IMSD: permeable soils).

interventions.landscape: Hard-rock areas with a weathered or fractured zone and falling water levels, in semi-arid and dry sub-humid climates; gently sloping cropland with wells downstream. Not where the water level after the monsoon is within 3 m of the ground: there is no room in the aquifer and the land waterlogs (CGWB; asked of the community, since the CoRE Stack has no depth-to-water layer yet).
interventions.suits: aquifer == 'hard_rock' and nz(soge_stage) >= 70 and rainfall in ['semi_arid', 'dry_subhumid'] and not (known(wl_post_monsoon) and wl_post_monsoon < 3)
interventions.avoid_note: Saline aquifer: recharge water mixes with saline groundwater.
interventions.caution: Silt seals the bed within a few years; desilt and treat the catchment. Check the strata: over massive rock with no weathered zone, water evaporates instead of recharging.
interventions.site_spec: Percolation tanks: on second- or third-order streams with catchments of about 2.5–8 km² (250–800 ha), land slope 3–5%, permeable weathered or fractured rock or alluvium beneath the tank, and a water table deeper than 3 m after the monsoon; the tank should normally empty by February (CGWB)
interventions.site_check: Revised against the CGWB manual and the Gujarat IWMP manual, which agree: the spreadsheet catchment (10–40 ha) is that of a small pond, not a percolation tank. Depth to water is part of the landscape fit, asked of the community.

interventions.name: Sub-surface dykes (underground bandharas)
interventions.what: An impermeable wall dug across a stream bed down to bedrock, holding groundwater in the sand and gravel upstream; it keeps wells beside the stream wet into summer without surface evaporation.
interventions.where: Stream or river beds with sandy fill over shallow bedrock
interventions.landscape: Seasonal rivers and wide nalas with sandy beds in hard-rock or coastal areas; drinking-water wells near the stream.
interventions.avoid_note: No river or upstream inflow through the micro-watershed.

interventions.name: Diversion-based irrigation
interventions.what: Small weirs that divert part of a perennial or long-flowing stream into gravity channels to fields, without pumps or large storage; a traditional system in hill areas.
interventions.where: Hill streams that flow beyond the monsoon
interventions.landscape: Hilly, sub-humid and humid tribal areas with streams that flow into rabi: forest-fringe and rainfed-rice micro-watersheds (for example Koraput, Godda).
interventions.suits: terrain == 'hilly' and rainfall in ['dry_subhumid', 'humid'] and (river_present >= 1 or n_upstream >= 1)
interventions.avoid_note: Streams do not flow long enough after the monsoon.
practice: Hill streams in Odisha and Jharkhand: diversion-based irrigation promoted by NGOs such as PRADAN and by state minor-irrigation programmes

interventions.name: Continuous contour trenches (CCT)
interventions.what: Trenches dug along the contour on uncultivated slopes; they stop sheet runoff, hold soil and moisture for grass and saplings, and recharge the aquifer below.
interventions.where: Ridges and upper slopes, non-cultivated land
interventions.site_spec: Ridges and steep slopes of 10–25%, non-cultivated land

site_rules.note: Gujarat: not below 10% (use contour bunds) or above 25%; Tripura: 10–30%; PRADAN: trenches above 8%. The spreadsheet range (1–10%) is that of bunds.

site_rules.partial: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping

interventions.landscape: Ridges and upper slopes under scrub, open forest or barren commons; the first step of ridge-to-valley treatment in hard-rock watersheds.
interventions.avoid_note: Almost no uncultivated land to trench.
interventions.caution: On slopes over 25% or in shallow soils use staggered trenches; avoid trenching dense natural forest.
practice: Watershed Organisation Trust (WOTR), Ahmednagar: ridge-to-valley treatment starting with CCT on hill slopes
interventions.site_check: Slope revised: every source puts contour trenches on 10–25% (up to 30%) slopes.

interventions.name: Staggered contour trenches (SCT)
interventions.what: Short trenches in a staggered pattern on steeper slopes, where continuous trenches would be unstable.
interventions.site_spec: Ridges and steep slopes of 10–25% (paper, Table 1)

site_rules.partial: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping

interventions.landscape: Hill slopes and ridges in forest-fringe and pastoral micro-watersheds.
interventions.site_check: Slope confirmed by the Gujarat manual and the Tripura guidelines.

interventions.name: Water absorption trenches (WAT)
interventions.what: Deep trenches at the foothills, where hill runoff reaches farmland; they intercept runoff, recharge the aquifer and protect fields from erosion.
interventions.where: Foothills, at the break of slope

site_rules.partial: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping

interventions.landscape: Micro-watersheds where hills meet farmland (both hill and plain or gentle-slope land present).
interventions.site_check: No published source found for these numbers; kept from the spreadsheet.

interventions.name: Trench-cum-bund networks (TCB)
interventions.what: Lines of trenches with the dug soil formed into a bund below, on gentle slopes and fallows; they harvest sheet runoff for recharge. The paper's Mala Khera (Bhilwara) plan projects that a TCB network protects about 13 ha of downstream crops and one well.
interventions.where: Gentle slopes, fallows and field edges

site_rules.accepted: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping

interventions.landscape: Semi-arid hard-rock micro-watersheds with gentle slopes, fallows and well-irrigated fields below.
interventions.caution: TCBs lose much of their storage to evaporation (paper, Table 3); they work for recharge, not storage.
practice: Foundation for Ecological Security (FES), Mandalgarh (Bhilwara, Rajasthan): TCBs in the paper's Mala Khera plan
interventions.site_check: No published source found for these numbers; kept from the spreadsheet.

interventions.name: Contour, graded and field bunds
interventions.what: Earthen bunds on farm boundaries along the contour (in low rainfall and permeable soils, to hold water) or with a slight grade (in higher rainfall and clayey soils, to drain excess safely); they keep soil and moisture on the field.
interventions.site_spec: Broad slopes 6–10% on farm boundaries: contour bunding, graded bunding, ditching (paper, Table 1)

site_rules.note: IMSD: contour bunding below 6%; Gujarat: not above 10%; PRADAN: field bunding below 3%.

site_rules.accepted: Single kharif, single non-kharif, double, triple cropping
site_rules.not_accepted: Trees/forest; Built-up; water in any season
Rocky, very shallow soils: stone bunds instead
site_rules.note: Contour bunds hold water on the field and are not suited to poorly drained clays (CGWB).

interventions.landscape: Rainfed cropland on gentle slopes: contour bunds in semi-arid areas, graded bunds in sub-humid and humid areas and on black clay soils. Contour bunds where rainfall is normally below 800 mm and the soil drains well; graded bunds, which lead excess water away, in wetter areas and on poorly drained clays (CGWB).
interventions.site_check: Slopes confirmed (IMSD, Gujarat, PRADAN). Rainfall decides contour or graded bunds (landscape); soil added as a site layer.

interventions.name: Stone bunding and stone terraces
interventions.what: Bunds of field stones around waste and fallow land and stony fields; they hold soil and let water through, and bring degraded land back into use.
interventions.where: Broad slopes (6–10%) off farm, around waste and fallow land
interventions.site_spec: Broad slopes 6–10% off farm: stone bunding around waste and fallow lands (paper, Table 1)

site_rules.accepted: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping

interventions.landscape: Stony, sloping rainfed land and fallows: dryland and forest-fringe micro-watersheds where farmland is being abandoned.
interventions.site_check: Slope consistent with the Gujarat contour bund limit (10%); other rows from the spreadsheet.

interventions.name: Bench terraces
interventions.what: Level steps cut into steep cultivated slopes; they stop erosion and hold water for rice and vegetables in hills.
interventions.site_spec: On-farm bench terracing on ridges and steep slopes (paper, Table 1)
interventions.landscape: Hill farming in humid and sub-humid tribal areas (for example Koraput, the Eastern Ghats and the Chhotanagpur plateau).
interventions.suits: terrain == 'hilly' and rainfall in ['dry_subhumid', 'humid'] and f_crop >= 0.2

interventions.name: Diversion and drainage-soakage channels
interventions.what: Channels from the foothills to a stream that carry excess hill runoff around fields, preventing inundation and gullying; soakage channels also let part of it infiltrate.
interventions.where: Foothills to the nearest stream, along field edges
interventions.site_spec: Diversion drains start at the foothills and end in a stream (paper, Table 1)

site_rules.accepted: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping

interventions.landscape: Farmland below hills in humid and sub-humid areas, and canal commands or plains with waterlogging and flooding.
interventions.site_check: No published source found for these numbers; kept from the spreadsheet.

interventions.name: In-situ moisture conservation (ridges and furrows, broad beds, mulching)
interventions.what: Field practices that keep rain where it falls: conservation furrows, ridge-and-furrow and broad-bed-and-furrow layouts, dead furrows, residue mulch and deep summer ploughing.
interventions.landscape: Rainfed dryland in semi-arid and dry sub-humid climates, especially black (vertisol) and red soils with dry spells during kharif.
practice: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming (Rythu Sadhikara Samstha): year-round soil cover, mulching in Anantapur's dry farms

interventions.name: Farm ponds (unlined)
interventions.what: Dug ponds on a farmer's field that store runoff for one or two protective irrigations during kharif dry spells and for rabi nursery or vegetables. The paper scores sites by catchment area, natural depression and distance to an upstream drainage line, and projects the number of fillings and irrigation cycles.
interventions.where: On farm, at the lowest corner of the field, slopes up to 5%, fed by field runoff
interventions.site_spec: Farm ponds: at the lowest point of the field, on slopes up to 5%, with a catchment of 1–5 ha (up to 14 ha on red soils) and low-infiltration soils over 1 m deep; line the pond on sandy and red soils (CRIDA)

site_rules.note: A farm pond sits at the lowest corner of the field and takes field runoff; on a larger stream it fills with silt and its bund is breached. The spreadsheet allowed orders 2–6.
CRIDA: 1–5 ha for black soils and 1–14 ha for red soils; IMSD: under 2 ha.

site_rules.accepted: Single kharif, single non-kharif, croplands, shrub/scrub, barren, double cropping
site_rules.not_accepted: Trees/forest; triple cropping; Built-up; water in any season

site_rules.note: Low-infiltration soils over 1 m deep hold water; sandy and red soils lose 40–50% to seepage unless lined (CRIDA).

interventions.landscape: Rainfed farms with dry spells in kharif, on gentle land with fine-textured soils that hold water; most useful where groundwater is scarce or saline. Pair with recharge works upstream (the paper's integrated planning delineates the upstream area that feeds a pond within the 120-day monsoon).
interventions.caution: In over-exploited blocks, ponds (especially lined ones) are often filled from borewells and used as storage of groundwater, which speeds depletion (Prasad et al. 2022). Ponds in hard rock need upstream recharge to fill reliably.
practice: Utthan, Bhavnagar (Gujarat) and FES, Anugul (Odisha): farm and community ponds in the paper's village plans
interventions.site_check: Revised against CRIDA (Reddy et al. 2012) and IMSD.

interventions.name: 5% model pits
interventions.what: A pit dug in the lowest corner of each paddy field, taking about 5% of its area; it catches runoff and seepage, saves the transplanted crop in dry spells and recharges groundwater.
interventions.where: On farm, upland and medium-land paddy fields
interventions.site_spec: Farm pond (5% model): broad slopes, catchment < 2 ha (paper, Table 1)

site_rules.note: PRADAN: medium uplands with a unidirectional slope, patches of at least 4 ha.

site_rules.accepted: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping, barren, shrub/scrub, trees/forest

interventions.landscape: Rainfed rice uplands in the sub-humid east (Chhotanagpur plateau, Eastern Ghats): Jharkhand, Odisha, West Bengal.
practice: PRADAN in Jharkhand and West Bengal: the 5% model for rainfed paddy uplands
interventions.site_check: Placement confirmed by PRADAN; numeric rows from the spreadsheet.

interventions.name: 30×40 model
interventions.what: Uplands divided into 30 × 40 ft plots, each with a small pit at its lowest corner and bunds around it; the whole slope is treated so that most rain infiltrates, reviving upland cultivation and tree crops.
interventions.site_spec: 30x40 model on upland slopes of 3–8%, between staggered trenches above and field bunds below (PRADAN)

site_rules.accepted: Single kharif, single non-kharif, double, triple cropping, barren, shrub/scrub

interventions.landscape: Degraded rainfed uplands in the sub-humid east and in dryland plateaus, especially land left fallow.
interventions.suits: f_slopy >= 0.2 and rainfall in ['dry_subhumid', 'humid'] and (degr_frac >= 0.01 or f_barren + f_shrub >= 0.1)
practice: PRADAN, Purulia (West Bengal) and Jharkhand: the 30×40 model for upland development
interventions.site_check: Slope revised against PRADAN (30x40 model on 3–8% uplands).

interventions.name: Community ponds and new tanks (incl. Amrit Sarovar)
interventions.what: Village ponds of about a hectare on a second- or higher-order drainage line, used for irrigation, livestock, fish and recharge, maintained by a user group.
interventions.where: Drainage line, gentle land, 10–40 ha catchment

site_rules.accepted: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping

site_rules.note: Same seepage reasoning as for farm ponds (CRIDA).

interventions.landscape: Villages with few waterbodies that hold water into rabi, livestock and fishery needs, on gentle land; in the paper's Baragotha (Anugul) plan a community pond fills about 12 times a monsoon.
interventions.caution: Site it where runoff reaches it but floods will not breach it; agree on users and maintenance before digging.
practice: FES, Anugul (Odisha): community pond in the paper's Baragotha plan
interventions.site_check: No published siting numbers found; kept from the spreadsheet. Mission Amrit Sarovar sets a water spread of at least 1 acre and about 10,000 m³ of storage, which a 10–40 ha catchment fills at 600 mm rainfall and 15% runoff.

interventions.name: Traditional runoff harvesting: johads, nadis, khadins, bandharas
interventions.what: Earthen crescent bunds (johads), village ponds (nadis), runoff-farming bunds (khadins) and diversion weirs (bandharas, phad systems) built and managed by communities, revived with local knowledge.
interventions.where: Drainage lines and valley floors in dry regions
interventions.site_spec: Khadins/johads on broad slopes (Table 1); nadis and bandharas on stream order 3+ (paper, Table 1)
interventions.landscape: Semi-arid and arid areas with short, intense monsoons: Rajasthan (johads, nadis, khadins) and the Deccan (bandharas).
interventions.avoid_note: Humid climate: other structures fit better.
practice: Tarun Bharat Sangh, Alwar (Rajasthan): community-built johads that revived seasonal rivers
Seva Mandir, Udaipur: anicuts and pasture with village institutions

interventions.name: Dug-well and borewell recharge
interventions.what: Runoff from fields or roofs led through a silt trap and filter into an open well or around a borewell, recharging the aquifer that the well draws on.
interventions.where: Existing wells on farms and in villages
interventions.landscape: Hard-rock areas where farms irrigate from dug wells and water levels fall in summer: groundwater-irrigated and orchard micro-watersheds in over-exploited or critical blocks. Not where the water level after the monsoon is within 3 m of the ground: there is no room in the aquifer and the land waterlogs (CGWB; asked of the community, since the CoRE Stack has no depth-to-water layer yet).
interventions.suits: aquifer == 'hard_rock' and nz(share_groundwater_irrigated) + nz(share_tree_crops) >= 0.15 and nz(soge_stage) >= 70
interventions.caution: Filter well: polluted runoff (pesticides, dung) goes straight into the aquifer.
practice: Saurashtra (Gujarat): farmers' well-recharge movement
Aga Khan Rural Support Programme (India) in Gujarat: well recharge in coastal and hard-rock areas

interventions.name: Recharge pits, soak pits and recharge shafts
interventions.what: Pits and shafts filled with gravel that let runoff and grey water reach permeable layers; shafts pierce a clay cap in alluvium. Bhungroo-type systems store excess monsoon water underground in waterlogged fields for rabi use.
interventions.where: Farm corners, village lanes, schools, low spots that waterlog

site_rules.accepted: Croplands; single kharif, single non-kharif, double and triple cropping

site_rules.not_accepted: Clay or Black without a permeable layer within reach
site_rules.note: Pits need permeable strata near the surface; shafts are dug through a clay layer to reach them (Gujarat; CGWB).

interventions.landscape: Alluvial plains with a clay layer, settlements and waterlogged low spots; peri-urban villages with paved surfaces. Not where the water level after the monsoon is within 3 m of the ground: there is no room in the aquifer and the land waterlogs (CGWB; asked of the community, since the CoRE Stack has no depth-to-water layer yet) Shafts suit most where the water level after the monsoon is deeper than 8 m (Gujarat IWMP manual).
interventions.suits: aquifer == 'alluvium' or nz(share_peri_urban) >= 0.1 or (known(wl_post_monsoon) and wl_post_monsoon >= 8)
interventions.caution: Arsenic and fluoride areas (for example Ballia's Ganga–Ghaghara alluvium): recharge only clean water and test wells.
practice: Naireeta Services, Gujarat: Bhungroo systems that store excess monsoon water underground
interventions.site_check: Soil added as a site layer (Gujarat, CGWB); depth to water is part of the landscape fit, asked of the community; other rows from the spreadsheet.

interventions.name: Rooftop rainwater harvesting
interventions.what: Roof water stored in tanks for drinking or led to recharge pits; mandatory for new buildings in many states.
interventions.landscape: Peri-urban villages and towns, hilly villages with poor wells, and places where groundwater is saline or fluoride-affected (stored roof water for drinking).

interventions.name: Desilting, with silt taken to fields
interventions.what: Removing silt from tanks and ponds to restore storage, and spreading the fertile silt on farms; done by the community or with machines after the waterbody dries.
interventions.landscape: Tanks and ponds in eroding catchments (sloping land, high runoff, degraded farmland) whose storage has fallen; fields nearby that benefit from silt.
interventions.caution: Test silt for contamination near towns; do not dig through the clay bed; treat the catchment or the silt returns in a few years.
practice: DHAN Foundation (Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh): tank-user associations that desilt and manage tanks
Kudimaramathu (Tamil Nadu) and Mission Kakatiya (Telangana): state tank-desilting drives with farmer participation

interventions.name: Restoring inlet and supply channels
interventions.what: Clearing, re-cutting and protecting the channels that bring runoff or canal water into a tank, and removing obstructions such as roads, fields or walls built across them.
interventions.where: Feeder channels of tanks and ponds
interventions.landscape: Tanks with large catchments that no longer fill, in hard-rock tank-irrigated areas and canal tails.
practice: DHAN Foundation: restoring supply channels in tank cascades

interventions.name: Repairing bunds, sluices and waste weirs
interventions.what: Strengthening and raising tank bunds, repairing or replacing leaking sluices and outlets, and rebuilding waste weirs so that floods pass without breaching.
interventions.landscape: Older tanks that lose water early or breached in recent years.

interventions.name: Protecting waterbody beds and catchments from encroachment
interventions.what: Demarcating the full tank level and the bed in revenue records, removing encroachments, notifying waterbodies under the wetland rules and keeping a buffer free of building.
interventions.where: Waterbody beds, foreshores and feeder channels
interventions.landscape: Peri-urban and intensively farmed areas where beds are farmed or built on.

interventions.name: Restoring tank cascades
interventions.what: Treating a chain of tanks along a stream as one system: restoring the links between them so that surplus from one fills the next, and sharing water across villages.
interventions.where: Chains of tanks on one drainage line
interventions.landscape: Hard-rock tank-irrigated landscapes of the Deccan and south India (for example Ananthapur and Chittoor).
practice: DHAN Foundation: cascade-level tank development (Vayalagam)

interventions.name: Deepening a pocket of the pond for summer water
interventions.what: Digging one deeper section of a shallow pond (or a separate dug-out beside it) so that some water lasts through summer for animals and fish, with a ramp or trough for cattle.
interventions.where: Village and headwater ponds that dry by February
interventions.landscape: Pastoral and dryland villages where animals depend on ponds in April–June.

interventions.name: Lining farm ponds
interventions.what: Plastic (geomembrane) or clay lining of farm ponds in permeable soils so that stored water lasts long enough for protective irrigation.
interventions.where: Farm ponds in sandy, gravelly or fractured ground
interventions.landscape: Light-textured soils and fractured rock where unlined ponds lose water within weeks; only where groundwater is not over-exploited.
interventions.avoid_note: Over-exploited or critical block: lined ponds are typically filled from borewells and add to depletion.
interventions.caution: Lining removes the recharge an unlined pond provides; subsidise only with an undertaking not to fill from borewells.

interventions.name: Pasture and commons restoration
interventions.what: Protecting village commons (social or physical fencing), seeding native grasses and legumes, soil and water works, and rotational grazing rules agreed by the village; restores fodder and infiltration.
interventions.where: Village commons, grazing land, degraded scrub
interventions.landscape: Pastoral and dryland villages with open commons under heavy grazing.
practice: Foundation for Ecological Security (Rajasthan, Odisha, Andhra Pradesh): commons restoration with village institutions
Seva Mandir, Udaipur: pasture land development

interventions.name: Assisted natural regeneration and community forest management
interventions.what: Protecting degraded forest so rootstock regenerates, gap planting with native species, and community forest-rights management plans that set harvest and grazing rules.
interventions.landscape: Forest-fringe micro-watersheds with tree-cover loss or degradation; tribal areas with community forest rights.
practice: Community forest rights management by gram sabhas in Odisha and Maharashtra (for example Mendha Lekha, Gadchiroli)

interventions.name: Community fire management
interventions.what: Fire lines cleared before the dry season, village fire watchers, controlled burning where traditional, and rules against setting fire for fresh grass or mahua collection.
interventions.landscape: Dry deciduous forest-fringe areas with frequent fires (Eastern Ghats, central India).

interventions.name: Agroforestry, bund plantations and orchards (wadi)
interventions.what: Trees on bunds and field edges, small fruit-tree orchards with intercrops on degraded or fallow land (the wadi model), and fodder trees; they add income, organic matter and soil cover.
interventions.landscape: Rainfed farms with fallows or degraded land, tribal areas, and farms near markets for fruit.
interventions.suits: degr_frac >= 0.01 or f_barren + f_shrub >= 0.1 or nz(share_tree_crops) >= 0.1
practice: BAIF: the wadi (tree-based farming) model with tribal families in Gujarat and Maharashtra

interventions.name: Riparian buffers and streambank planting
interventions.what: Native trees, grasses and bamboo along streams and river banks; they stabilise banks, filter silt and keep the stream shaded.
interventions.landscape: Micro-watersheds with a river or many streams, eroding banks or sand mining.

interventions.name: Village crop-water budgeting and water security plans
interventions.what: The village estimates water available from rain, surface storage and groundwater, and the water its crops need, and agrees a crop plan for the season. The paper's impact projection shows that at landscape scale changing the cropping pattern did far more than new structures (about 92% against 8% of the deficit in one micro-watershed).
interventions.landscape: Groundwater-irrigated and dryland micro-watersheds with a water-balance deficit or over-exploited groundwater; also where new structures are planned, to set expectations.
practice: Watershed Organisation Trust (WOTR), Maharashtra: water budgeting with village water stewardship
FES India Observatory: crop water budgeting tool
Atal Bhujal Yojana: gram-panchayat water security plans

interventions.name: Shifting to less water-intensive crops
interventions.what: Moving part of the area from paddy, sugarcane or banana to millets, pulses, oilseeds or short-duration varieties. The paper's crop evapotranspiration (kharif): paddy 262 mm, pigeon pea 325 mm, cotton 281 mm, maize 180 mm, millet 150 mm, sorghum 136 mm, green gram 127 mm; shifting a quarter of the area saved about 9% of crop water.
interventions.where: Cropland, decided by farmers and the village
interventions.landscape: Groundwater-irrigated and canal areas in over-exploited or critical blocks; rice and sugarcane in semi-arid hard rock.
interventions.caution: Needs assured procurement or markets for the new crops; savings vanish if saved water expands the irrigated area.
practice: Odisha Millets Mission (including Koraput)
Haryana's Mera Pani Meri Virasat: incentives for leaving paddy
Hiware Bazar (Maharashtra): village ban on water-intensive crops such as sugarcane

interventions.name: Drip and sprinkler irrigation, with a cap on irrigated area
interventions.what: Drip for orchards, sugarcane and vegetables, sprinklers for field crops; cuts application losses. Water is saved for the aquifer only if the irrigated area is not expanded.
interventions.landscape: Groundwater-irrigated farms and orchards in semi-arid hard rock (for example the Warud–Morshi orange belt in Amravati, Ananthapur's groundnut and horticulture).
interventions.caution: Efficiency gains are often used to expand area and increase total consumption (the irrigation-efficiency paradox, Grafton et al. 2018); pair with water budgeting or area caps.

interventions.name: Underground pipelines and lined field channels
interventions.what: Replacing earthen field channels from tanks, canals or wells with buried pipes or lined channels, reducing seepage and evaporation and letting water reach tail fields.
interventions.landscape: Canal and tank commands with long field channels and tail-end shortages; seepage-driven waterlogging.

interventions.name: Rice water saving: SRI, alternate wetting and drying, direct seeding
interventions.what: System of Rice Intensification, alternate wetting and drying in irrigated rice, and direct-seeded rice instead of puddled transplanting; less water per tonne of rice.
interventions.landscape: Rice-growing micro-watersheds: canal and groundwater-irrigated rice, and rainfed rice in the sub-humid east.
practice: PRADAN with SHG federations in Jharkhand and Odisha: SRI paddy

interventions.name: Protective irrigation at critical crop stages
interventions.what: Using stored pond or tank water for one or two irrigations at sowing, flowering or grain filling during dry spells, rather than for a full second crop; the paper sizes the cycles a pond supports (for example 4 cycles of 50 mm for 3 ha of paddy).
interventions.landscape: Rainfed farms with mid-season dry spells, where ponds or tanks hold water through kharif.

interventions.name: Community groundwater rules and monitoring
interventions.what: Farmers measure rainfall and water levels in their wells, share the data, and agree rules: spacing and depth limits for new borewells, no-borewell zones near drinking-water sources, sharing of existing wells, and crop choices for the season.
interventions.landscape: Hard-rock aquifers in over-exploited or critical blocks with dense borewells.
practice: Andhra Pradesh Farmer Managed Groundwater Systems (APFAMGS): hydrological monitoring by farmers in drought-prone districts
ACWADAM with partner NGOs: participatory groundwater management
Hiware Bazar (Maharashtra): village ban on new borewells

interventions.name: Water user associations and agreed sharing (warabandi)
interventions.what: Tank and canal users form or revive an association that schedules turns, maintains channels and collects fees; rotations reach tail-end fields.
interventions.landscape: Canal and tank commands with unequal distribution or unused stored water.
practice: DHAN Foundation: tank farmers' associations
Pani panchayats in Odisha

interventions.name: Drainage and conjunctive use against waterlogging
interventions.what: Surface and sub-surface drains, pumping shallow groundwater alongside canal water (conjunctive use), bio-drainage with trees, and less water-intensive crops in seepage areas.
interventions.landscape: Canal commands and floodplains with high water tables and waterlogged fields.

interventions.name: Rabi pulses and oilseeds on rice fallows
interventions.what: Zero-till or relay sowing of lentil, chickpea, linseed, mustard or grass pea after kharif rice, using residual moisture with one protective irrigation at most.
interventions.where: Rice fields left fallow after kharif
interventions.landscape: Rainfed rice areas of the sub-humid east with land fallow in rabi (Jharkhand, Odisha, eastern UP).

interventions.name: Soil organic matter and balanced nutrients
interventions.what: Composting, green manure, residue retention, tank silt, natural farming practices and soil-test-based fertiliser; more organic matter holds more water in the root zone.
interventions.landscape: Farms with low nitrogen or organic carbon, and rainfed farms where water-holding capacity limits crops.
practice: Andhra Pradesh Community-managed Natural Farming

interventions.name: Drought contingency crop plans and seed
interventions.what: Short-duration and drought-tolerant varieties, contingency crops for delayed monsoon, community seed banks, and crop insurance; from the district agriculture contingency plans.
interventions.landscape: Rainfed dryland in semi-arid and dry sub-humid climates with frequent drought or delayed sowing.

interventions.name: Fodder banks, troughs and herd management
interventions.what: Fodder plots and banks, silage, stall-feeding of improved animals, cattle troughs fed from a source protected from contamination, and agreed grazing calendars; reduces pressure on commons and water.
interventions.landscape: Pastoral and mixed villages with high livestock density or summer water stress for animals.

interventions.name: Protecting and recharging drinking-water sources
interventions.what: Recharge structures above drinking-water wells and borewells, no-irrigation-pumping zones around them, village water safety plans and testing; Jal Jeevan Mission's source-sustainability works.
interventions.landscape: Villages with low piped-water coverage or sources that fail in summer, especially in over-exploited hard-rock blocks.
practice: Gram Vikas, Odisha: village piped water with community management

interventions.name: Safe water for saline, fluoride or arsenic areas
interventions.what: Community treatment plants (for example reverse osmosis or defluoridation), arsenic-removal units or deeper safe aquifers, and stored roof water for drinking.
interventions.landscape: Saline aquifers, fluoride belts (hard rock in Rajasthan and Andhra Pradesh) and arsenic in the Ganga alluvium (for example Ballia).

interventions.name: Flood adaptation: raised platforms, tolerant rice, drainage and safe water
interventions.what: Raised homestead and hand-pump platforms, submergence-tolerant rice (Swarna-Sub1), clearing drainage lines, maintaining embankments and early warning.
interventions.landscape: Floodplains of large rivers (for example the Ganga–Ghaghara around Ballia).
practice: Megh Pyne Abhiyan, north Bihar: safe drinking water and sanitation in flood-prone villages

interventions.name: Keeping recharge zones and waterbodies free of building
interventions.what: Mapping recharge zones, drainage lines and waterbodies in village and town plans, and keeping them out of new layouts; mandatory rainwater harvesting in new buildings.
interventions.landscape: Peri-urban micro-watersheds where farmland and waterbodies are being built on.

interventions.name: Inland fishery in seasonal ponds and tanks
interventions.what: Stocking fingerlings of fast-growing carps matched to how long the water lasts, leases to SHGs or fishers' cooperatives, and sharing rules with irrigators so that fish and irrigation coexist.
interventions.where: Ponds and tanks holding water 4 months or more
interventions.landscape: Waterbodies that hold water into rabi in villages that already fish; sub-humid and humid areas.

interventions.name: Settlement-wise, equitable planning with SHGs
interventions.what: Planning settlement by settlement so that marginalised hamlets get structures first (as CSOs do with tools such as Commons Connect), SHG and producer groups for water-based livelihoods, and land development of SC/ST farmers' plots.
interventions.landscape: Villages with high Scheduled Tribe or Scheduled Caste shares, low assets and weak access to irrigation.
practice: Commons Connect: digital participatory planning used by CSO field teams (paper)
PRADAN, FES and others: hamlet-level planning with women's groups

interventions.name: Solar and community lift irrigation, where groundwater is safe
interventions.what: Solar pumps or community lift schemes on rivers, ponds and shallow aquifers to irrigate a rabi crop, run by user groups; only where groundwater or surface water is under-used.
interventions.where: Farms near streams, ponds or shallow wells
interventions.landscape: Sub-humid eastern India and floodplains with safe groundwater and single-season cropping (rice fallows).
interventions.avoid_note: Over-exploited or critical block: free solar power accelerates pumping.
